e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5.aim: Black avoids the main lines with an offbeat defence, usually at the cost of time or space.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5.White: Castle, then c3 and d4: a broad centre punishes passive setups.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5.Black: Keep e5 firm, finish development, and avoid falling further behind.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6.aim: The Berlin: Black hits e4 and steers for a solid structure or the Berlin endgame.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6.White: Castle and Re1 or d4; in the endgame, use the kingside majority and Black's awkward king.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6.Black: Trade queens when allowed, lean on the bishop pair, and keep the structure compact.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5.aim: The Classical Defense puts the bishop on its best diagonal before White's centre arrives.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5.White: Castle, then c3 and d4 to gain time on the c5 bishop.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5.Black: ...Nf6 or ...Nge7, keep the bishop active, and hit back with ...d5.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5.aim: The Schliemann: Black attacks e4 at once to open the f-file.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5.White: Nc3 and d3 or d4: keep control and open lines against Black's king.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5.Black: Develop fast, take on e4, and use the f-file before White consolidates.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6.aim: The Old Steinitz holds e5 with a pawn: solid, but cramped.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6.White: d4 and Nc3 for space, then increase the pressure on e5.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6.Black: ...Bd7 and ...Nf6; give up e5 with ...exd4 only when forced, then play actively.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4.aim: Bird's Defense trades knights to ease the pressure on e5, leaving a pawn on d4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4.White: Nxd4 exd4, castle, and attack the d4 pawn with c3.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4.Black: Develop quickly and use the d4 pawn to cramp White.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4.aim: White keeps the pressure on c6 and e5 while Black chooses a set-up.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4.White: Castle, then c3 and d4 for a broad centre.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4.Black: Pick a plan: ...Nf6 for the main lines, ...d6 to hold e5, or ...b5 to gain space.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6.aim: The main Ruy: Black develops and hits e4, White castles and fights for d4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6.White: O-O, Re1, c3 and d4; the bishop on b3 keeps pressure on f7 and d5.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6.Black: ...Be7 or ...Nxe4, then ...b5 and ...d6, aiming for ...d5 or ...c5 breaks.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7.aim: The Closed Ruy: a slow fight over e5 and d4 with long manoeuvres.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7.White: Re1, Bb3, c3, h3 and d4; Nbd2-f1-g3 for the kingside and a4 against the queenside.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7.Black: ...b5, ...d6, ...O-O, then ...Na5 and ...c5, or ...Re8 and ...Bf8 to hold e5.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.aim: The Marshall: Black gives a pawn for a fierce, long-lasting kingside attack.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.White: Take the pawn, defend with d4, Re1 and g3, and return material if it kills the attack.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.Black: Pile on with ...Bd6, ...Qh4 and ...Bg4; the attack has to keep moving.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.aim: The Breyer reroutes the knight to d7 so it supports e5 and frees the c-pawn.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.White: Nbd2-f1-g3, Bc2, and a4 or a d5 clamp.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Qe2.aim: The Worrall Attack: the queen backs up e4 so the rook can go to d1.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Qe2.White: c3, d4 and Rd1 for central pressure.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Qe2.Black: ...b5, ...d6 and ...O-O, then ...Bg4 or ...Na5 against the b3 bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 Qe2.aim: The Wormald Attack: the queen backs up e4 so the rook can go to d1.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 Qe2.White: c3, d4 and Rd1 for central pressure.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 Qe2.Black: ...b5, ...Be7 and ...d6, then ...Bg4 to pin and pressure d4.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4.aim: The Open Ruy: Black takes e4 for active pieces, accepting a looser structure.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4.White: d4 and Re1 to win the pawn back, then target the c5 and e6 squares and the d5 pawn.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4.Black: ...b5, ...d5 and ...Be6 for active pieces; keep the e4 knight well supported.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5 Bb3.aim: The Arkhangelsk: the bishop on b7 hits e4 and the long diagonal.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5 Bb3.White: c3 and d4, or Re1 and a4 to question the queenside.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5 Bb3.Black: ...Bc5 or ...Be7, then pressure e4 and d4 with active pieces.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Bc5.aim: The Møller: the bishop goes to c5 early, inviting c3 and d4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Bc5.White: c3 and d4 with tempo on the bishop.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Bc5.Black: ...b5 and ...d6, keeping the bishop active on the a7-g1 diagonal.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O d6.aim: Black holds e5 with ...d6 after castling, letting Bxc6 and d4 test the structure.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O d6.White: Bxc6+ and d4 to open the centre against the doubled pawns.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O d6.Black: Recapture towards the centre and use the bishop pair once lines open.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 d3.aim: White protects e4 quietly and avoids sharp theory for a slow manoeuvring game.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 d3.White: c3, Nbd2-f1-g3 and a gradual kingside build-up.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6.aim: The Modern Steinitz holds e5 with ...d6, ready to break the pin with ...b5.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6.White: c3, d4 and O-O for a big centre; Bxc6 when it damages Black's pawns.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6.Black: ...Bd7 and ...Nge7, or the sharp ...f5 (Siesta), keeping e5 firm.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5.aim: Black kicks the bishop early, gaining space but committing the queenside.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5.White: Bb3, then a4 to hit the b5 pawn, or c3 and d4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5.Black: ...Bb7, ...Bc5 or ...Na5 to trade off the b3 bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6.aim: The Exchange Ruy: White damages Black's pawns, aiming for a favourable endgame.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6.White: d4 and trade pieces; the 4-v-3 kingside majority can make a passed pawn.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6.Black: Use the bishop pair and open lines; keep pieces on and avoid simple endgames.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5.aim: Both bishops aim at the enemy f-pawn; the fight is over d4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5.White: c3 and d4 for a big centre, or d3 and a slow build-up with Re1 and Nbd2-f1-g3.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5.Black: ...Nf6, ...d6 and ...O-O; hit back with ...d5 when White's centre isn't ready.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4.aim: The Evans Gambit: a pawn for time, so c3 and d4 build the centre with tempo.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4.White: c3, d4, O-O and pressure on f7 and the open centre.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4.Black: Keep the pawn only if it's safe; returning it to finish development is often best.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6.aim: The Two Knights: Black counterattacks e4, inviting sharp play.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6.White: Ng5 to hit f7, d4 for open play, or d3 for a calm game.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6.Black: Meet Ng5 with ...d5 and keep developing; gambit lines give Black quick activity.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Be7.aim: The Hungarian Defense: passive but solid, avoiding every sharp line.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Be7.White: d4 for space, then d5 to cramp Black.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Be7.Black: ...d6, ...Nf6 and ...O-O; look for ...c6 or ...f5 to free the game.

e4 e5 f4 exf4.aim: White trades the f-pawn for a strong centre and fast development.
e4 e5 f4 exf4.White: d4, Bc4, O-O and the f-file; regain f4 when convenient.
e4 e5 f4 exf4.Black: Hold the pawn with ...g5, or return it with ...d5 for free development.

e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3.aim: White plays for d4 and a lead in development; Black tries to keep the pawn.
e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3.White: d4, Bc4 and O-O, then open the f-file against f7.
e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3.Black: ...g5 or ...d6 to keep the pawn, or ...d5 to give it back and develop.

e4 e5 f4 exf4 Bc4.aim: The Bishop's Gambit lets the king go to f1 in return for fast development.
e4 e5 f4 exf4 Bc4.White: Nc3, d4 and Nf3 with tempo on Black's queen.

e4 e5 f4 d5.aim: Black strikes the centre instead of taking the gambit pawn.
e4 e5 f4 d5.White: Take on d5 and keep the extra pawn, developing safely.
e4 e5 f4 d5.Black: ...e4 or ...c6 to gain activity against White's loosened king.

e4 e5 f4 Bc5.aim: Black declines, using the bishop to stop White castling short.
e4 e5 f4 Bc5.White: Nf3, c3 and d4 to blunt the bishop.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4.aim: The Vienna Gambit opens the f-file and gains space with e5.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4.White: Push e5, then Nf3, d4 and play down the f-file.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4.Black: ...d5 at once to open the centre, using the knight on e4.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4.aim: White aims at f7 and keeps f4 in reserve.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4.White: d3, f4 or Nge2: open the f-file against Black's king.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4.Black: ...Nc6 and ...Bc5, or the sharp ...Nxe4 fork trick.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4.aim: The Frankenstein-Dracula: wild tactics where Black can give up a rook for activity.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4.White: Qh5 and the attack on f7; grab material only if it's safe.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4.Black: ...Nd6 and ...g6, then trap or chase White's queen and stranded knight.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3.aim: A quiet fianchetto aiming at d5 and the long diagonal.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3.White: Bg2, Nge2, O-O and a slow build-up with d3 and f4.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3.Black: ...d5 to free the game, then ...Bd6 and ...O-O.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6.aim: Symmetrical development; White chooses between f4 and a fianchetto.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6.White: f4 for gambit play, or g3 and Bg2 for a slow game.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 f4.aim: A wild gambit: White gives material for an attack on f7.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 f4.White: h4, Ng5 and d4, opening lines on Black's king.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 f4.Black: Keep the material and consolidate with ...d6 and ...Bg7.

e4 e5 Nc3 Bc5.aim: Black eyes f2 and keeps the setup flexible.
e4 e5 Nc3 Bc5.White: Nf3 and d4 to open the centre while ahead in development.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6.aim: A classical centre fight: White presses d5 and the queenside, Black stays solid.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6.White: Bg5, e3, Rc1 and Bd3; in Carlsbad structures push b4-b5 (the minority attack).
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6.Black: ...Be7, ...O-O and ...Nbd7, then free the game with ...c5 or ...e5.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5.aim: The Exchange: a Carlsbad structure, White's minority attack against Black's kingside chances.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5.White: Bd3, Qc2, Rb1 and b4-b5 to leave Black a weak c-pawn.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5.Black: ...Ne4 and ...f5 for kingside play; meet b5 with ...c6 exchanges.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 c5.aim: The Semi-Tarrasch: Black hits d4 and accepts an open centre.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 c5.White: cxd5 and e4 for a big centre, then d5 or a kingside attack.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 c5.Black: Trade pieces and attack the centre with ...cxd4 and ...Nc6.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5.aim: The Tarrasch: an isolated d-pawn in exchange for active pieces.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5.White: g3 and Bg2 to hit d5; trade pieces and blockade on d4.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5.Black: Rooks to the c- and e-files, ...Be6, and ...d4 at the right moment.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4.aim: The Accepted: Black takes c4 to gain time; White builds a centre and wins it back.
d4 d5 c4 dxc4.White: e3 or e4, Bxc4 and O-O; aim for d5 or a kingside attack.
d4 d5 c4 dxc4.Black: ...c5, ...a6 and ...b5, with free development through ...Nc6 and ...Bb7.

d4 d5 c4 e5.aim: The Albin: a pawn for a cramping d4 pawn and quick piece play.
d4 d5 c4 e5.White: g3, Bg2 and Nbd2; return the pawn if needed and target d4.
d4 d5 c4 e5.Black: ...Nc6, ...Be6 and often ...O-O-O with a kingside pawn push.

d4 d5 c4 Nc6.aim: The Chigorin: Black trades pawns for active pieces.
d4 d5 c4 Nc6.White: Nf3 and cxd5 to win the centre and the bishop pair.

d4 d5 c4 Bf5.aim: The Baltic: Black develops the light bishop before ...e6.
d4 d5 c4 Bf5.White: Nc3 and Qb3 to hit b7 and d5.
d4 d5 c4 Bf5.Black: ...e6 and ...c6, accepting a queen trade on b3.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2.aim: The Closed Catalan: Black keeps d5 solid, White builds slow pressure.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2.White: Nf3, O-O, Qc2 and e4 to open the centre for the g2 bishop.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 dxc4.aim: The Open Catalan: Black takes c4; White wins it back with lasting pressure.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 dxc4.White: Nf3, O-O and Qc2 or Qa4+ to regain c4, then press the long diagonal.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 dxc4.Black: ...a6 and ...b5 or ...Nc6 to hold or return the pawn, then free the c8 bishop.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 Bb4+.aim: The Bogo-Catalan: Black swaps or misplaces White's dark-squared bishop.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 Bb4+.White: Bd2, Bg2 and Nf3, keeping the long-diagonal pressure.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 c5.aim: Black heads for Benoni-style play against the fianchetto.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 c5.White: d5, Nc3 and use the central majority.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3.aim: A Catalan reached through Nf3, after Black has committed to ...d5.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3.White: Bg2, O-O and Qc2, regaining c4 if Black takes it.

d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6.aim: Black attacks b2 straight away, testing the London's weak spot.
d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6.White: Nc3 (offering b2) or Qc1 and Nd2: development matters more than the pawn.
d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6.Black: Take on b2 only if it's safe; otherwise develop with ...Nc6 and ...d5.

d4 Nf6 Bf4 e6.aim: Black heads for a Queen's Indian setup aimed at e4.
d4 Nf6 Bf4 e6.White: e3, Nf3, h3, Bd3, c3 and Nbd2, then e4 or Ne5.

d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6.aim: Black sets up a Grünfeld or King's Indian against the London.
d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6.White: Nc3 and Nb5 ideas against c7, or e3, Nf3 and h3.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4.aim: A King's Indian setup against the London.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4.White: e3, h3, Be2, O-O and c3; then e4 or a queenside push.

d4 d5 Bf4 Bf5.White: e3, c4 and Qb3 to hit b7.

d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c6.aim: A Slav setup: solid and level.
d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 c6.White: Nf3, Bd3 or c4, aiming for e4.

d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 e6.aim: Black plays a Queen's Gambit-style setup with ...c5.
d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 e6.White: Nf3, c3, Nbd2 and Bd3, aiming for Ne5 and a kingside attack.
d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3 e6.Black: ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Bd6 to trade off the f4 bishop.

d4 d5 Bf4 c5.aim: Black hits d4 and b2 at once.
d4 d5 Bf4 c5.White: e3, c3 and Qb3 to neutralise ...Qb6.

d4 d5 Nc3.aim: The Jobava London: aggressive, with Nb5 ideas against c7.
d4 d5 Nc3.White: Bf4, Nb5, e3, and sometimes O-O-O with a kingside push.
d4 d5 Nc3.Black: ...Na6 to cover c7, then ...c6 or ...c5 and ...Bd6.

d4 f5 Bf4.White: e3, Nf3, Bd3 and Nbd2, then e4 or a kingside attack.
d4 f5 Bf4.Black: ...b6 and ...Bb7 to control e4, then ...Be7 and ...O-O.

c4 e5.aim: A reversed Sicilian: White plays the Sicilian with an extra tempo.
c4 e5.White: Nc3, g3 and Bg2, then queenside expansion with Rb1 and b4.
c4 e5.Black: ...Nc6 and ...Nf6, then ...d5 or a ...f5 kingside push.

c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 g3.aim: The Closed English: White plays on the queenside, Black on the kingside.

c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6.aim: The Four Knights English: symmetrical development.
c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6.White: g3, Bg2 and O-O, then d4 to open the centre.

c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3.aim: After ...d5 and cxd5 it's a Dragon with colours reversed.
c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3.White: Bg2, Nf3, O-O, then a3 and b4 on the queenside.

c4 e5 Nc3 Bb4.aim: Black gives the bishop for c3 to double White's pawns.
c4 e5 Nc3 Bb4.White: Bg2 and open the position for the bishop pair.

c4 e5 Nc3 d6.aim: The Botvinnik setup: Black builds a broad kingside centre.
c4 e5 Nc3 d6.White: g3, Bg2, then e4 or Rb1 and b4.

c4 c5.aim: The Symmetrical English: a slow fight over d4 and d5.
c4 c5.White: Nc3, g3 and Bg2, then d4, or b3 and Bb2.

c4 Nf6 Nc3 d5.aim: An Anglo-Grünfeld: Black plays a Grünfeld against the English.
c4 Nf6 Nc3 d5.White: g3 and Bg2, pressing the long diagonal.

c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e4.aim: The Mikenas: White grabs the centre with e4 and e5.
c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e4.White: e5 and d4 for space, then attack any advanced Black pawn.
c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e4.Black: ...d5 and ...d4 for activity, then hit the centre.

c4 Nf6 Nc3 g6.aim: Black sets up a King's Indian against the English.
c4 Nf6 Nc3 g6.White: g3, Bg2, Rb1 and b4 for queenside play.

c4 c6.aim: Black prepares ...d5 with a Slav or Caro-Kann structure.
c4 c6.White: Nf3, e3, b3 and Bb2, or e4 for open play.

c4 c6 e4.aim: White switches to an open game with e4; after the exchanges it's a Panov-style fight.
c4 c6 e4.White: Develop fast with Nc3 and Nf3, and play against Black's queenside pawns.
c4 c6 e4.Black: ...Nf6 and ...Nxd5, then ...g6 and ...Bg7 or ...Nc6 for active pieces.

c4 e6.White: Nf3, g3, Bg2, O-O, then b3 and Bb2.

c4 f5.aim: A Dutch setup against the English.
c4 f5.White: g3, Bg2, Nc3 and d4, then the e4 break.

e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3.aim: The Open Sicilian: White's space and development against Black's c-file and central majority.
e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3.White: Choose an attack: Be3 and O-O-O, Bg5 and f4, or Be2 and f4.
e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3.Black: Counterattack on the queenside with ...a6, ...b5 and rooks on the c-file.

e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6.aim: The Najdorf: ...a6 controls b5 and keeps ...e5, ...e6 and ...b5 all available.
e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6.White: Be3, f3, Qd2 and O-O-O (English Attack), or Bg5 and f4.
e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6.Black: ...e5 or ...e6, then ...b5 and ...Bb7; attack on the c-file and queenside.

e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6.aim: The Dragon: the g7 bishop rakes the long diagonal towards White's queenside.
e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6.White: Be3, f3, Qd2 and O-O-O, then h4-h5 and Bh6 to swap the Dragon bishop.
e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6.Black: ...Nc6, ...O-O and ...Rc8, with ...Rxc3 sacrifices; race with ...a5 or ...b5.

e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6.aim: The Scheveningen: a small, flexible centre with pawns on e6 and d6.
e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6.White: The Keres Attack with g4-g5, or Be2, O-O and f4.

e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6.aim: The Classical: natural development, keeping every option open.

e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5.aim: The Sveshnikov: Black accepts a hole on d5 for active pieces and the bishop pair.
e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5.White: Bg5 and Nd5, then occupy d5 and target the backward d6 pawn.
e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5.Black: ...b5, ...Bg7 or ...Be7, and ...f5 to break White's grip.

e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 e5.aim: The Kalashnikov: Black kicks the knight, conceding d5 for activity.
e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 e5.White: Nb5, N1c3 and Nd5; c4 to clamp the centre.

e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6.aim: The Accelerated Dragon: fianchetto without ...d6, keeping ...d5 in one move.
e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6.White: c4 for the Maróczy bind, or Nc3, Be3 and Bc4.

e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6.aim: The Taimanov: flexible, with ...Qc7 and ...a6 keeping the structure open.
e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6.White: Nc3, Be3, Qd2 and O-O-O, or Be2 and O-O.

e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6.aim: The Kan: ...a6 covers b5 and the queen goes to c7.
e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6.White: Bd3, O-O and c4 for a Maróczy-style bind.

e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6.aim: The Four Knights Sicilian: fast development, often with ...Bb4.
e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6.White: Ndb5 or Nxc6, and e5 to kick the knight.

e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Bb5+.aim: The Moscow: White trades bishops and builds a calm centre.
e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Bb5+.White: c3 and d4, Re1 and a slow central build-up.

e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5.aim: The Rossolimo: White pressures c6 and may double Black's pawns.
e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5.White: O-O, Re1, then Bxc6 with c3 and d4.

e4 c5 c3.aim: The Alapin: White aims for a classical pawn centre.
e4 c5 c3.White: d4 and cxd4 for a full centre, then simple development.
e4 c5 c3.Black: ...Nf6 or ...d5 to hit the centre before it settles.

e4 c5 Nc3.aim: The Closed Sicilian: slow play aimed at the kingside.
e4 c5 Nc3.White: g3, Bg2, d3, f4 and f5, or Bc4 in the Grand Prix.

e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3.aim: The Smith-Morra: a pawn for development and open files.
e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3.White: Nxc3, Nf3, Bc4, O-O, Qe2 and Rd1: pressure on d6 and f7.
e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3.Black: Develop solidly with ...Nc6, ...e6, ...d6 and ...Be7; return the pawn if needed.

e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4.aim: The Winawer: after e5 and a3, White gets the bishop pair and doubled c-pawns.
e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4.White: Qg4 against g7, or Nf3, a4 and play for the bishops.
e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4.Black: ...c5, ...Ne7 and ...Qc7 or ...Qa5: attack d4 and the doubled pawns.

e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6.aim: The Classical: Black pressures e4; White chooses e5 or Bg5.
e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6.White: e5 and f4 for space, or Bg5 lines with play on the kingside.
e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6.Black: ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6 against d4, or ...dxe4 after Bg5.

e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4.aim: The Rubinstein: Black gives up the centre for solid, easy development.
e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4.White: Nf3, Bd3, O-O and Qe2, then c3 and d5 or a kingside push.
e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4.Black: ...Nd7, ...Ngf6 and ...Be7, then free the game with ...c5.

e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2.aim: The Tarrasch: White avoids pins on c3 and keeps c3 for a pawn.
e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2.White: Ngf3, Bd3, O-O and c3; aim to isolate Black's d-pawn.
e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2.Black: ...c5 for an isolated-pawn game, or ...Nf6, ...Nfd7 and ...f6.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3.aim: The Advance: a locked centre where Black attacks d4 and White guards it.
e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3.White: Bd3, O-O and a kingside attack, keeping d4 supported.
e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3.Black: ...Qb6, ...Bd7 and ...f6 against e5, or ...Nge7-f5 to hit d4.

e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5.aim: The Exchange: a symmetrical, open structure.
e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5.White: Quick development, then c4 or Bd3 and kingside play.
e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5.Black: ...Bd6, ...Nf6 and ...O-O; the c8 bishop is free now.

e4 e6 d3.aim: A King's Indian Attack against the French.
e4 e6 d3.White: Nd2, Ngf3, g3, Bg2, O-O, then e5 and a kingside attack.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4.aim: Black gives up the centre to develop freely; the bishop or a knight comes out next.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4.White: Use the space: Nf3, Bd3 or Bc4, and O-O.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5.aim: The Classical: the bishop develops with tempo, White uses extra space.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5.White: Ng3 and h4-h5 to push the bishop back, then Bd3 and O-O-O.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7.aim: The Karpov: ...Ngf6 next without allowing doubled pawns.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7.White: Ng5 or Nf3 and Bd3, playing for a space edge.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6.aim: Black allows doubled pawns in return for open lines.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6.White: c3, Bd3 and Ne2, then target the damaged pawns.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6.Black: ...Bd6 or ...Bf5, castle, and use the open e- or g-file.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5.aim: The Advance: White gains space; Black's bishop must get out before ...e6.
e4 c6 d4 d5 e5.White: Nf3, Be2, O-O and c4, or h4 to harass the bishop.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5.aim: The Exchange: a symmetrical structure; White looks to the kingside.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5.White: Bd3, c3, Bf4 and Qb3 against b7.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4.aim: The Panov: an isolated-pawn fight where White attacks and Black blockades.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4.White: Nc3, Nf3 and Bg5, then a kingside attack using the d4 pawn.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4.Black: ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...Be7, blockade on d5 and trade pieces.

e4 c6 d4 d5 f3.aim: The Fantasy: White supports e4 with a pawn to keep the full centre.
e4 c6 d4 d5 f3.White: Nc3, Be3 and Qd2, or e5 for space.
e4 c6 d4 d5 f3.Black: ...e6 or ...dxe4 and ...e5 to strike the centre.

e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3.aim: The Two Knights: quick development, centre kept flexible.
e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3.White: h3, recapture on f3 with the queen, then d4 and Bd3.
e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3.Black: ...Bg4xf3, ...e6 and ...Nf6: solid with a sound centre.

e4 c6 d3.aim: A King's Indian Attack against the Caro-Kann.
e4 c6 d3.White: Nd2, Ngf3, g3, Bg2, O-O and Re1.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4.aim: The Austrian Attack: White grabs space and threatens e5.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4.White: Nf3, Bd3, O-O, then e5 or f5 with an attack.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4.Black: ...Bg7, ...O-O, then ...c5 or ...Na6 to strike the centre.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3.aim: White plans Qd2 and Bh6 with a kingside attack.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Ng4.aim: Black hits the bishop at once to gain the bishop pair or time.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Ng4.White: Bg5 and h3, or keep the bishop with Bg3.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Ng4.Black: ...h6, ...g5 and ...Bg7, playing on the dark squares.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Nf3.aim: The Classical: solid development, White keeps a modest space edge.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Nf3.White: Be2, O-O, h3, then a4 or Re1.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Bg5.aim: The Byrne: White harasses the knight and prepares Qd2.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Bg5.White: Qd2 and f3 or Nf3, keeping Bh6 ideas.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Bd3.aim: White avoids Nc3 and keeps c3 for a pawn.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Bd3.White: c3 and Nf3, then a solid centre.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Bd3.Black: ...e5 and ...d5 to equalise in the centre.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 f3.aim: White supports e4 with f3, heading for a Sämisch-style setup.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 f3.White: Be3, Qd2 and c4 for a space-grabbing bind.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 g3.aim: A quiet fianchetto against the Modern.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 g3.White: Bg2, Ne2, O-O, then c3 or c4.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Bg5.aim: White eyes e7 early, provoking ...h6 or ...c5.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Bg5.White: Qd2 and Nc3, with O-O-O ideas.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 c3.aim: White supports d4 with c3 and plans f4 for a broad centre.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 d6 Be3.aim: White plans Qd2 and a kingside attack.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 d6 Be3.White: Qd2, f3, then O-O-O or h4-h5.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 d6 f4.aim: The Austrian: a big centre, threatening e5.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 d6 f4.White: Nf3, Bd3 and e5 for space.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 c6.aim: The Gurgenidze: Black aims for ...d5 and a light-square setup.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 c6.White: f4 and e5 to lock the centre.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 d6 Nf3.aim: Calm development that often turns into a Pirc.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3.aim: White develops calmly, keeping a solid centre.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3.White: Be2 or c3, O-O and a modest space edge.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 c4.aim: White grabs space with c4 for a bind.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 c4.White: Nc3 and Be3, keeping the bind.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Bc4.aim: White aims the bishop at f7.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 f4.aim: Black hits the big centre at once with ...d5.

e4 g6 d4 d6.aim: The Hippopotamus: small steps, then counterpunches.
e4 g6 d4 d6.White: Develop naturally and expand, without over-committing.
e4 g6 d4 d6.Black: ...a6, ...b6, ...Bb7, ...Nd7 and ...e6, waiting for the right break.

e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6.aim: Black hits e5 at once; White decides how to support it.
e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6.White: Nf3 and Be2 for solidity, or c4 and f4 for maximum space.
e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6.Black: ...dxe5 or ...Bg4, then ...e6 and ...c5 against the centre.

e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3.aim: The Modern: White supports e5 with a piece rather than more pawns.
e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3.White: Be2, O-O and c4, keeping e5.

e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4.aim: White grabs space with c4, with f4 next in the Four Pawns Attack.
e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4.White: f4 and Nf3, or exd6 for an open game.

e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Bc4.aim: The Balogh: White aims at f7 with Bc4-b3.
e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Bc4.White: Qh5 or Nf3 for an attack.

e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 c4.aim: The Chase: White chases the knight early.
e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 c4.White: c5 and Bc4 or Nc3, using the space.

e4 Nf6 Nc3.White: exd5 or e5 with quiet development.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5.aim: The queen on a5 pins the c3 knight and stays out of harm's way.
e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5.White: d4, Nf3, Bc4, Bd2 and O-O.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6.aim: The queen on d6 eyes the centre and b4.
e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6.White: d4, Nf3, then g3 or Ne5.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd8.White: d4, Nf3 and Bc4 for a space edge.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6.aim: Black recaptures later with the knight.
e4 d5 exd5 Nf6.White: d4 or c4, holding d5 for a while.
e4 d5 exd5 Nf6.Black: ...Nxd5 with quick development, or gambit with ...c6 or ...e6.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Bg4.aim: The Portuguese Gambit: Black develops quickly.
e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Bg4.White: f3 and c4 to keep the pawn.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 c4 e6.aim: The Icelandic Gambit: a pawn for open lines.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 c4 c6.aim: Black offers a pawn for development.
e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 c4 c6.White: d4 and Nc3 to keep the centre.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 Bb5+.aim: White disrupts Black's development with a check.
e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 Bb5+.White: Bc4 and try to keep the d5 pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4.aim: The Classical Petrov: a symmetrical, very solid position.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4.White: d4, Bd3, O-O and c4, or Nc3 with O-O-O.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4.Black: ...d5, ...Be7, ...O-O and ...Nc6; keep the e4 knight supported.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7.aim: The Cochrane: a piece for two pawns and an exposed king.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7.White: d4, Nc3 and Bc4, attacking the king.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7.Black: Consolidate with ...c5 or ...Be7, returning material if needed.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4.aim: The Steinitz Attack opens the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3.aim: Three Knights: White develops before taking on e5.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4.aim: White offers e4 for gambit play.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 Nbd7.aim: The Lion: Black holds e5 with pieces in a compact shell.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 Nbd7.White: Bc4, O-O, Re1 and a4 for space.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 e5.aim: The Lion reached through a Pirc move order.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 e5.White: Nf3, Bc4 and O-O, then Re1.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4.aim: The Exchange: Black gives up the centre for piece play.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4.White: Nxd4, Nc3, Be3, Qd2 and O-O-O.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7.aim: The Hanham: the knight supports e5.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6.aim: Black pressures e4 and keeps e5.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6.White: Nc3, or dxe5 Nxe4 for open play.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f5.aim: The Philidor Countergambit: sharp play on the f-file.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e.aim: The Classical: Black hits the centre with ...e5; once it locks, each side attacks its own wing.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e.White: Close with d5, then b4 and c5 for a queenside breakthrough on c7.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e.Black: ...Nh5 or ...Ne8, then ...f5, ...f4 and ...g5 for a kingside storm.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e.aim: The main line: ...Nc6 provokes d5, sending the knight to e7 for the kingside attack.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e.White: After d5 Ne7, push b4, c5 and Nd2-c4 to break through.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e.Black: ...Ne8 or ...Nd7, then ...f5, ...f4 and ...g5: a race against White's queenside play.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e.aim: The Petrosian: White closes early; ...a5 slows White's queenside expansion.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e.White: Bg5 to pin, then b4 or c5 when ready.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f3.aim: The Sämisch: f3 supports e4 and prepares Be3, Qd2 and a kingside storm.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f3.White: Be3 and Qd2, often O-O-O with g4 and h4.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f3.Black: Strike quickly with ...c5 or ...e5, or ...Nc6, ...a6 and ...b5.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f4.aim: The Four Pawns Attack: maximum space, which Black must undermine at once.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f4.White: e5 to drive the knight back and break Black's position open.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f4.Black: ...c5 and ...e6 to open lines against the over-extended pawns.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Be2 O-O.aim: The Averbakh: Be2 and often Bg5 restrain ...e5 and pin down Black's kingside.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Be2 O-O.White: Bg5 and Qd2 with h4 ideas; meet ...e5 or ...c5 with d5.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Be2 O-O.Black: ...c5 or ...e5, often after ...h6 or ...Na6, with play on the dark squares.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 h3.aim: The Makogonov: h3 stops ...Ng4 and ...Bg4 and prepares Be3 and g4.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 h3.White: Be3 and g4 to clamp the kingside before ...f5.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 Nf3 d6 Bg5.aim: The Smyslov: Bg5 develops before e4, keeping the centre flexible.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 Nf3 d6 Bg5.Black: ...c5, or ...h6 and ...e5 to free the game.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 g3.aim: The Fianchetto: White's g2 bishop makes Black's kingside attack much harder.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 g3.White: Keep the centre solid and press on the queenside and long diagonal.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 g3.Black: Panno (...Nc6, ...a6, ...Rb8, ...b5) or Yugoslav ...c5: play on the queenside.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4.aim: White avoids theory with a London setup.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4.White: e3, h3, Be2, O-O and c3, then e4 or a queenside push.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4.aim: The Nimzo-Indian: Black pins c3 to fight for e4, ready to trade bishop for knight.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4.White: Choose Qc2, e3 or a3; aim for the bishop pair and the centre.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4.Black: ...O-O, ...d5 or ...c5, and ...b6; target doubled c-pawns if they appear.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2.aim: The Classical: White avoids doubled pawns, spending time with the queen.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2.White: a3 to win the bishop pair, then e3 or Nf3.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2.Black: ...O-O, then ...d5 or ...c5: develop fast while the queen is on c2.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3.aim: The Rubinstein: solid development with Bd3 and Nf3 or Ne2.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3.White: Bd3, Nf3, O-O, then a3 to gain the bishop pair.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 a3.aim: The Sämisch: White takes the bishop pair, Black targets the doubled c-pawns.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 a3.White: f3 and e4 for a big centre.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Nf3.aim: Flexible development, keeping g3 or Qb3 options.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qb3.aim: The Spielmann: the queen covers c3 to avoid doubled pawns.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 f3.aim: The Kmoch: White prepares e4 directly.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 f3.White: a3 and e4 for a big centre.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 f3.Black: ...d5 or ...c5, hitting the centre before it forms.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6.aim: The Queen's Indian: Black controls e4 from b7, solid and flexible.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6.White: g3 and Bg2, or a3 and Nc3 to fight for e4.

d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+.aim: The Bogo-Indian: a check to swap the dark-squared bishops.
d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+.White: Bd2 or Nbd2, then g3 and Bg2.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5.aim: The Exchange: White's big centre against Black's pieces and ...c5.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5.White: e4, then Nf3 or Bc4, Be3, O-O and Rc1; push d5 when possible.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5.Black: ...Bg7, ...c5 and ...Nc6, with ...Qa5 or ...Bg4 to attack d4.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Nf3.aim: White develops before deciding on the centre.
d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Nf3.White: Qb3 or e3 and Be2, then a solid centre.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg7 Qb3.aim: The Russian: White pressures d5 and grabs the centre.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Bf4.aim: White pressures c7 and avoids the main lines.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Qb3.aim: An early queen: pressure on d5.

d4 Nf6 c4 g6 g3 d5.aim: Black hits the centre before White's bishop settles.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4.aim: The Main Line: Black takes c4, aiming for ...Bf5 and ...e6.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4.White: a4 to stop ...b5, then e3 and Bxc4, or Ne5.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6.aim: The Semi-Slav: a rock-solid centre with ...dxc4 ideas.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 a6.White: e3, b3 or c5 to stop ...b5.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3.aim: A quiet line: White protects c4.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3.White: Nc3, Bd3, O-O, Qc2 and e4.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5.aim: The Exchange Slav: a symmetrical structure.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 dxc4.aim: Black takes c4 and White builds the centre with e4.

d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6.aim: The Modern Benoni: Black's queenside majority and open e-file against White's central majority.
d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6.White: Nc3, e4 and Be2 or Bd3, then the e5 break or f4.

d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5.aim: The Benko: Black gives a pawn for open a- and b-files.
d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5.White: Keep the pawn, develop, and blunt the pressure.
d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5.Black: ...Bxa6, ...g6 and ...Bg7, with rooks on a8 and b8.

d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e5.aim: The Czech Benoni: a closed centre and slow manoeuvring.
d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e5.White: e4, Nc3, Be2, then h3 or g4.

d4 c5 d5 e5.aim: The Old Benoni: a closed centre and slow manoeuvring.
d4 c5 d5 e5.White: e4, Nc3 and Nf3, then play on the queenside.

d4 f5.aim: The Dutch: Black fights for e4 with the f-pawn and aims at the kingside.
d4 f5.White: Fianchetto, c4 and Nc3, then e4 to break Black's grip.
d4 f5.Black: ...Nf6 and ...e6 or ...g6; hold e4 and attack with ...Qe8-h5.

d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 d5.aim: The Stonewall: Black locks e4 with pawns, leaving a hole on e5.
d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 d5.White: Nf3, O-O, b3 and Ba3 to swap dark bishops, then Ne5.

d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 Be7.aim: The Classical Dutch: a flexible ...d6 setup.

d4 f5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 g6.aim: The Leningrad: a King's Indian-style setup with f5.
d4 f5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 g6.White: Nf3, O-O, c4, Nc3 and d5.

d4 f5 Bg5.White: e3, Bg3 and h4 against the advanced pawns.

d4 f5 e4.aim: The Staunton Gambit: a pawn for development.
d4 f5 e4.White: Nc3, Bg5, then f3 or d5.

d4 f5 Nf3.aim: A London-style setup against the Dutch.
